title: How to Build a Portfolio Website with Carrd
why: A portfolio needs to look good, load fast and point visitors to one action: hire me. That's what Carrd is built for.
sections: Hero: your name, what you do, one line on who you do it for
Selected work: 6–9 best pieces in a gallery (quality over quantity)
About: a short paragraph and a photo
plan_reason: A custom domain (yourname.com) and a contact form are what make a portfolio look professional, and both need Pro Standard.
tips: Use a Gallery element with lightbox so work opens full-screen.
Link each project to a longer case study (Behance, Notion or another Carrd site).
Put your contact button in the hero and again at the bottom.

title: How to Make an Art Commissions Page on Carrd
why: Commission carrds are one of the most popular Carrd uses. One page holds your price sheet, examples, TOS and how to order.
sections: Price sheet: types (headshot, half-body, full-body) with example images
Terms of service: payment, refunds, what you will and won't draw
How to order: form or Ko-fi/PayPal link
plan_reason: An order form that collects references and details needs the Form element (Pro Standard). On the free plan you can link to Ko-fi or a Google Form instead.
tips: Put your TOS before the order button. It prevents most disputes.
Keep a single 'Status' line at the top so you only edit one thing when you open or close.
Show real finished examples for every price tier.

title: How to Build a Link-in-Bio Page with Carrd (Linktree Alternative)
why: A Carrd link-in-bio looks like your brand instead of a template, and one yearly Pro plan costs less than most monthly link tools.
sections: Primary link buttons (3–6, most important first)
Featured content: latest video, product or newsletter sign-up
plan_reason: Pro Lite removes the Carrd branding. Choose Pro Standard if you also want your own domain or a newsletter sign-up form.
tips: Keep one clear main link at the top and change it weekly.
Use a narrow content width (around 20–24rem) so it looks like an app on phones.
Add GA4 (Pro Standard) to see which links people click.

title: How to Build a Startup Landing Page with Carrd
why: Indie hackers have launched thousands of products on Carrd because you can go from idea to live page with sign-ups in about an hour.
sections: Primary CTA: waitlist sign-up or buy
plan_reason: Waitlist forms, a custom domain and GA4/Meta Pixel tracking all need Pro Standard, and a landing page is pointless without them.
tips: Test one headline at a time. With one page, it's easy to see what changed.
Send the form to a thank-you section so you can count sign-ups in analytics.
Build a separate Carrd site for each idea you test.

title: How to Make a Resume Website with Carrd
why: A one-page resume site on your own domain helps you stand out from PDF applicants, and Carrd makes it quick.
plan_reason: A custom domain (firstlast.com) is the main reason to upgrade here. Free works for a quick version.
tips: Match the site's headline to the roles you're applying for.
Link a PDF copy for recruiters' applicant tracking systems.
Put the URL in your email signature and LinkedIn.

title: How to Build a Musician Website on Carrd
why: Musicians need a hub for music, shows and merch that they can update in minutes. Carrd covers it on one page.
sections: Hero with latest release + listen buttons
plan_reason: Playable Spotify or Apple Music embeds and a booking form both need Pro Standard.
tips: Lead with one release, not your whole catalogue.
Link tour dates to your ticketing page instead of retyping them.
A clean EPK section makes it easier to get booked.

title: How to Build a Photography Portfolio with Carrd
why: Photos should carry the page. Carrd's full-bleed images and gallery lightboxes keep everything else out of the way.
plan_reason: Booking forms and a custom domain need Pro Standard. Also check image limits on your plan.
tips: Compress images before uploading to keep the page fast.
Use hidden sections as category 'pages'.
Put a booking button on every section.

title: How to Build a Freelancer Website with Carrd
why: Clients want to know three things quickly: what you do, proof you can do it, and how to hire you. One Carrd page covers all three.
plan_reason: A custom domain and contact form are the minimum for being taken seriously by clients.
tips: Put starting prices on the page so you get fewer tyre-kickers.
Embed a Calendly link via Embed (Pro Standard) for instant bookings.

title: How to Make an Event or Wedding Website with Carrd
why: Events need one page with the date, place, schedule and an RSVP, live quickly and cheap enough to throw away afterwards.
plan_reason: An RSVP form and a map or countdown embed need Pro Standard. Add Pro Plus if you want password protection for private guest lists.
tips: Send RSVPs to a spreadsheet via webhook.
Add a map embed so guests don't need a separate link.

title: Is Carrd Good for a Small Business Website?
why: Plenty of cafés, salons, trades and service businesses only need hours, location, services and a way to get in touch. Carrd does that for a small yearly fee.
plan_reason: A custom domain and contact form are must-haves for a business. Pro Standard includes both.
tips: Add a tap-to-call button (tel: link) for mobile visitors.
Keep your name, address and phone exactly the same as on your Google Business Profile.

title: How to Make a Fandom / BYF Carrd (Aesthetic Bio Guide)
why: Carrd is the standard for fandom bios: about me, BYF/DNI, interests and socials, styled however you like.
plan_reason: The free plan covers most bio carrds. Upgrade to Pro Standard only for music embeds, custom fonts via code, or animated widgets.
tips: Use hidden sections as tabs (/#about, /#dni) to keep it tidy.
Pick 2–3 colors and one decorative font for a consistent look.
Credit resource creators for any dividers or pngs you use.

title: How to Build a Newsletter Sign-up Page with Carrd
why: A focused sign-up page usually converts better than your newsletter platform's default page, and you control it.
sections: Headline: what readers get + how often
plan_reason: The Signup form with Mailchimp/ConvertKit integration needs Pro Standard.
tips: One field only: email.
Show a real past issue. Being specific gets more sign-ups.
